stem.text: Let \( g(x) = - 2 x^{3} - 21 x^{2} - 72 x - 5 \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether g has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = -3 \) and at \( x = 5 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = -3 \), g has a relative maximum because \( g'(-3) = 0 \) and \( g''(-3) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 5 \), g has no relative extremum because \( g'(5) = -432 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( g'(x) = - 6 x^{2} - 42 x - 72 \), which factors as \( g'(x) = - 6 \left(x + 3\right) \left(x + 4\right) \).
\( g'(-3) = 0 \), so \( x = -3 \) is a critical point, while \( g'(5) = -432 \ne 0 \), so \( x = 5 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test g has a relative maximum at \( x = -3 \). At \( x = 5 \) the first derivative is not zero, so g has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.

options.label: At \( x = -3 \), g has an absolute maximum because \( g'(-3) = 0 \) and \( g''(-3) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 5 \), g has no relative extremum because \( g'(5) = -432 \ne 0 \).
options.derivation: the relative extremum from the second derivative test extended to an absolute one with no argument that it is the only critical point, which it is not
